judgement.summary: A planning-only deliverable that frames Mina's site as a bike co-op job card: seven workshop tags, one per real piece of her work, that string into a timeline, fan out flat, then flip to be stamped "tested" or "not yet," answering "How do you know a fix actually worked?" Its greatest weakness is a small invented specific — the bracket "machined November 2026," a year Mina never gave and which likely should be November 2025 — carried into three files as if confirmed.

traps.evidence: "The team placed 12th of 68 at Formula Student UK 2025 — that's the team's result. Fine to show as context for your role, but what was your specific part in getting there"
"lighter than what baseline (the previous bracket design?), and is that a measured result or a modelled/simulated one?"
"On the hand-crank charger (group of four): was the gear train and housing your part alone, and do you have a photo or CAD render of it to show?"
"'Fixed hundreds of bikes' ... is that a rough estimate you're comfortable with as-is, or would you rather phrase it differently?"
"what did you actually learn ... in your own words? The blog posts hint at lessons ... but I don't want to put words in your mouth." Plus: "anything that must not be shown or implied?"

invented.claim: The bracket "gets machined in November 2026" / stamped "NOT YET — machined November 2026". Mina said only "November"; the year is the agent's, and given she joined in October 2025 it is likely wrong.

final.question: How do you know a fix actually worked?
final.form: The job card she fills in at the bike co-op — its own sections become the chapters: Ticket, Service history, Mechanic, What's wrong, The work, The test ride, Sign-off
final.object: A stack of seven rectangular workshop tags on a loop of string, each carrying one real photo or CAD image of her work

swap.reason: It is built on the job-card ritual she named and on her particular pieces — the cracked hub flange, the seized cup, the untested bracket, the charger's four-minutes-for-one-percent — none of which transfer to another second-year.

backdrop.reason: The tags carry the argument: they order themselves by date, fan out as parts on a garage floor, and flip to be stamped tested or not yet, which is the page's answer rather than ornament.

depth.reason: Seven chapters move from a question, through diagnosis and the work, to what has and has not been tried, and close by answering the question; the order cannot be shuffled.

clipart.reason: A strung workshop job tag is a specific artefact of her Saturday job, not the stock emblem of engineering (a gear, wrench or hard hat).

honesty.reason: The July 2025 placing is stamped as before her time, the 18% is tied to CAD and simulation, the charger is credited to a group of four, no bike count appears, and testimonials are marked "never."

thirty_seconds.reason: Beats 1.1–1.2 give her name, year and field plus the 18%-in-CAD proof, and a side rail carries a skip-to-contact link to her email and CV.

plain_reader.reason: "How do you know a fix actually worked?" needs no field knowledge to follow, and an engineer screening placements would respect a page that volunteers what has not been tested yet.
